title: Post-infarct ventricular septal defect and free wall rupture: pathology, hemodynamics and repair
subject: ss-ctvs
refs: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22e Ch 111 (Post-Infarction Mechanical Complications)
Kirklin/Barratt-Boyes Cardiac Surgery 4e Ch 13 (Ischemic Mechanical Complications)
ACC/AHA Guidelines for the Management of Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction

steps.say: Ventricular septal rupture complicates up to point five percent of transmural infarctions. It typically manifests three to seven days after ischemic injury, as dense coagulative necrosis weakens the necrotic septum. Neutrophilic infiltration dissolves structural collagen, predisposing the necrotic myocardium to sudden mechanical shear.
steps.tx: Acute **ventricular septal rupture** complicates 0.2 to 0.5 percent of acute infarctions, typically developing 3 to 7 days post-infarction. Severe **coagulative necrosis** and intense **neutrophilic infiltration** weaken the infarcted myocardium, leading to sudden mechanical structural disruption under left ventricular systolic pressures.

steps.say: Anatomy varies decisively based on coronary artery territory. Left anterior descending artery occlusion yields an anterior infarction and produces an apical VSD that is simple and direct. Inferior myocardial infarctions from right coronary occlusion produce basal posterior VSD defects that are tortuous and serpiginous.
steps.tx: An **anterior infarction** from left anterior descending artery occlusion produces an **apical VSD** that is typically direct and simple. In contrast, inferior wall infarction causes a complex, serpiginous **basal posterior VSD** that tracks irregularly through the necrotic posteroinferior interventricular septum.

left.title: Apical Septal Rupture
points: Associated with anterior infarction and LAD occlusion
Direct, simple defect located at cardiac apex
Technically easier surgical exposure and closure

right.title: Basal Posterior Rupture
points: Associated with inferior infarction and RCA or LCx disease
High operative mortality with difficult posterior exposure

steps.say: Sudden deterioration with acute biventricular failure heralds septal rupture. Auscultation reveals a harsh, loud holosystolic murmur with a palpable thrill along the left lower sternal border. Differentiating this quickly from acute mitral regurgitation is vital for immediate operative planning.
steps.tx: The classical presentation features acute hemodynamic collapse, rapid pulmonary edema, and **biventricular failure**. Bedside auscultation demonstrates a harsh, loud **holosystolic murmur** accompanied by a **palpable thrill** maximal over the left lower sternal border, distinguishing it clinically from acute mitral valve papillary muscle rupture.

steps.say: Echocardiography confirms the diagnosis and quantifies shunt magnitude. Color Doppler demonstrates left-to-right flow across the muscular septum with right ventricular volume overload. Transesophageal echocardiography defines defect margins and excludes concomitant papillary muscle disruption.
steps.tx: Bedside transthoracic and **transesophageal echocardiography** confirm the diagnosis, visualizing left-to-right flow across the muscular septum by **color Doppler**. Comprehensive imaging calculates the **left-to-right shunt** fraction, estimates right ventricular systolic pressure overload, and completely rules out concomitant ischemic papillary muscle rupture.

nodes.label: Sudden cardiogenic shock with new harsh systolic murmur
Demonstrate left-to-right shunt across ventricular septum
Initiate IABP counterpulsation and emergency surgical prep

steps.say: Insert an intra-aortic balloon pump immediately while preparing for surgery. Rapid deflation drops left ventricular afterload, decreasing the left-to-right shunt fraction. Counterpulsation augments coronary artery perfusion, stabilizing the failing biventricular myocardium prior to ventriculotomy.
steps.tx: Immediate **intra-aortic balloon pump** placement is crucial for preoperative patient stabilization. The dramatic **afterload reduction** decreases left ventricular systolic pressure, producing significant **shunt reduction** across the defect while simultaneously augmenting diastolic coronary perfusion pressure before emergency surgery in unstable patients.

rows: Maintains perfusion to ischemic non-infarcted myocardium
Reverses tissue hypoperfusion and end-organ acidosis

steps.say: Repair utilizes the David infarct exclusion technique through a left ventriculotomy. Open through the necrotic infarcted anterior or inferior wall without cutting healthy tissue. Secure a large bovine pericardial patch over the left ventricular side using pledgeted sutures.
steps.tx: Modern surgical repair employs the **infarct exclusion technique** of Tirone David via an open **left ventriculotomy** through infarcted myocardium. A tailored Dacron or **bovine pericardial patch** is sutured to healthy non-infarcted endocardium, excluding the necrotic zone from left ventricular pressure without requiring extensive debridement.

left.title: Infarct Exclusion Principle
points: Anchors patch to healthy left ventricular endocardium
Avoids tension on friable necrotic muscular tissue

right.title: Historical Direct Suture Repair
points: Sutures placed directly through friable necrotic muscle
High rate of catastrophic suture pull-through
Severe risk of immediate recurrent ventricular shunting

steps.say: Perform concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting to non-infarcted vessels whenever indicated. Bypassing stenotic vessels in non-culprit territories preserves remaining functional myocardium and enhances operative survival. The ventriculotomy is then closed securely over Teflon felt strips.
steps.tx: Executing **concomitant CABG** to bypass stenosed coronary arteries in **non-infarcted territories** improves immediate **operative survival** and preserves residual ventricular functional capacity. Bypassing non-culprit ischemic beds protects remaining myocardium during postoperative recovery and weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass in the intensive care unit.

nodes.label: Review coronary angiogram for non-infarcted territory stenosis
Construct vein or arterial bypass grafts to remote vessels
Close ventriculotomy over reinforced Teflon felt strips

steps.say: Free wall rupture is an even deadlier mechanical catastrophe occurring in one to two percent of infarctions. It manifests with acute tamponade, pseudoaneurysm, or sudden electromechanical dissociation. Emergency patch repair with biological glue rescues patients from fatal hemopericardium.
steps.tx: Acute left ventricular **free wall rupture** occurs in 1 to 2 percent of transmural infarctions, presenting catastrophically as acute **electromechanical dissociation** or fatal cardiac tamponade. Contained tears form a **pseudoaneurysm**, requiring emergency surgical repair utilizing Teflon-felt or bovine pericardial sutureless patch techniques with biological glue.

rows: Sudden cardiac arrest, EMD, fatal tamponade
Epicardial patch with bio-glue and pledgeted sutures
Urgent resection and patch reconstruction of neck
